dervis-irab:1-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بُعْثِرَتْ) Al-Zamakhsharī said: "بعثر and بحثر have one meaning; they are composed of البعث (raising) and البحث (searching) with a rāʾ joined to them. The meaning is: they were searched through and their dead brought out. [Sūrat] Barāʾa was called al-Mubaʿthira because it turned out (بعثرت) the secrets of the hypocrites." In al-Mukhtār: "بحثره فتبحثر, i.e. he scattered it and it was scattered. Al-Farrāʾ said: بحثر متاعه وبعثره, i.e. he dispersed it and turned some of it over onto other parts. Abū al-Jarrāḥ said: بحثر الشيء وبعثره, i.e. he extracted it and uncovered it."

* I'rab:
(إِذَا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ وَإِذَا الْكَواكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ وَإِذَا الْبِحارُ فُجِّرَتْ وَإِذَا الْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ، عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ) (إذا) is an adverb for future time, putting its protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) in the genitive and itself accusative by its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (السماء) is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb indicated by the one mentioned, and the clause (انفطرت) is explicative. The clause "انفطرت السماء" is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and the adverb is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the apodosis, which is (علمت). What follows is conjoined to it. (البحار) and (القبور) are the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb. The clause (علمت) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (علمت نفس) is a verb and its fāʿil, (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (أخّرت) [Translator's note: so in the source; it is (قدّمت) that is the ṣila, with (أخّرت) conjoined to it] has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما).
(يا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسانُ ما غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ) (يا) is a vocative particle; (أيّها) is the one addressed, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of the accusative by (يا); the hāʾ is for drawing attention; and (الإنسان) is a badal (substitute). (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (غرّك) is its khabar (predicate). (بربك) is attached to (غرّك), and (الكريم) is an adjective of (ربك). Ibn Jubayr and al-Aʿmash read ما أغرّك, so it may be that أن [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably ما] is interrogative, or that it is of wonder (taʿajjub). He, glory be to Him, said الكريم rather than any other of His beautiful names and attributes only because it is as though He, the Exalted, prompted him with the answer, so that he would say: "The generosity of the Generous deluded me."
(الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ) (الذي) is a second adjective of (ربك), affirming the lordship; the clause (خلقك) is the ṣila of (الذي); (فسوّاك) is conjoined to (خلقك), and likewise (فعدلك).
(فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ ما شاءَ رَكَّبَكَ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (ركبك); (ما) is redundant (zāʾida); the clause (شاء) is an adjective of (صورة), and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, i.e. شاءها (He willed it). The meaning is: He gave you a description in whatever form His will required, of beauty and ugliness, tallness and shortness, maleness and femaleness. (وعدلك) means: He made you of balanced stature, proportionate in form, without disparity. It may also be attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He assembled you while you are found in one of the forms. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be attached to (عدلك), with (أيّ) having the meaning of wonder, i.e. He balanced you in a wondrous form."
(كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ) (كلا) is a particle of rebuke and restraint, and (بل) is a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī) to the explanation of the real cause of their delusion. Al-Rāghib's wording: "بل here is for validating the second and cancelling the first, as though it were said: there is nothing here that requires anything to delude them regarding Him, the Exalted; rather, it is their denial that drove them to what they committed." (تكذبون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative and its fāʿil, and (بالدين) is attached to (تكذبون).
(وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحافِظِينَ كِراماً كاتِبِينَ) The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), confirming the disapproval, and the clause is a ḥāl from the wāw in (تكذبون), i.e. you deny while the scribes write everything that comes from you. The wāw may also be resumptive, the clause being resumptive, set out to inform them of that so that they may desist from what they are upon. (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb; (عليكم) is its fronted khabar; the lām is for emphasis; and (حافظين) is the noun of (إنّ), or it is an adjective of its noun, i.e. angels. (كراما) is a naʿt (adjective) of (حافظين), and (كاتبين) a second naʿt.
(يَعْلَمُونَ ما تَفْعَلُونَ) The clause is a third naʿt. (يعلمون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative and the wāw is its fāʿil; (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi; and the clause (تفعلون) is the ṣila, with the referring pronoun omitted, i.e. تفعلونه.
(إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ) The clause is resumptive, set out to answer an implied question, its implied form being "Why do they write that?" — as though it were said: so that He may recompense the righteous with bliss and the wicked with the Blaze. (إنّ) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (في نعيم) is its khabar. The clause (وإن الفجّار …) is conjoined to the preceding clause and parsed like it.
(يَصْلَوْنَها يَوْمَ الدِّينِ) The clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun, namely (لفي جحيم). (يصلونها) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw is its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; (يوم الدين) is an adverb attached to (يصلونها). The clause (يصلونها) may also be resumptive, set out to answer an implied question, its implied form being "And what will their affair come to in the Blaze?"
(وَما هُمْ عَنْها بِغائِبِينَ) He meant: they will roast in the Fire on the Day of Judgement, and they are not absent from it before that, i.e. in their graves.
(وَما أَدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ ثُمَّ ما أَدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ) The wāw is a conjunction. (ما) is an interrogative noun of disapproval, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (أدراك) is the khabar. (أدراك) is an imperfect verb [Translator's note: so in the source; أدراك is a past verb] with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, its implied form being "huwa", and the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi. (ما) is an interrogative noun whose meaning is to make terrible and great, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and (يوم الدين) is its khabar. The clause, suspended (muʿallaqa) by the interrogative, stands in place of the second object of (أدراك). Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Everything in the Quran with His saying ما أدراك, He has informed him of it; and everything in it with His saying وما يدريك, He has withheld it from him."
(يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئاً وَالْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ) (يوم) is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember). Abū al-Baqāʾ made it an adverb attached to something omitted, its implied form being "they will be recompensed". It was also read in the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ or as a badal from (يوم الدين). The clause (لا تملك) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; (نفس) is the fāʿil, its tanwīn being for generalization, i.e. every soul; and (شيئا) is a mafʿūl bihi. (الأمر) is a mubtadaʾ; (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to something omitted as a ḥāl, the tanwīn being a substitute for a clause; and (لله) is the khabar of (الأمر).

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجّار لفي جحيم» there is al-waṣl (conjoining). The discussion of waṣl and faṣl (conjoining and disjoining) has preceded. Among the requirements of waṣl present here is the agreement of the two clauses in being declarative or performative (khabariyya / inshāʾiyya), together with a connection, i.e. a common factor between them, which here is contrast.
2- In these two verses there is also the device of al-tarṣīʿ [Translator's note: the source prints الترجيع; the definition given is that of al-tarṣīʿ], a kind of rhymed prose (sajʿ): every word in the first half of the verse or the prose clause corresponds to its counterpart in metre, rhyme-letter and case-ending. Among what has come of it in poetry is the saying of Abū Firās:
وأفعالنا للراغبين كريمة ... وأموالنا للطالبين نهاب
(Our deeds towards those who seek us are generous, and our wealth is booty for those who ask.)
